events.title: Edward III and John II agree the Treaty of Brétigny
events.description: King Edward III of England and the captive John II of France agreed the Treaty of Brétigny, ending the first phase of the Hundred Years' War. Edward gave up his claim to the French crown for sovereignty over Aquitaine, Calais and Ponthieu.
events.html: King Edward III of England and the captive John II of France agreed the Treaty of Brétigny, ending the first phase of the Hundred Years' War. Edward gave up his claim to the French crown for sovereignty over Aquitaine, Calais and Ponthieu.

events.title: Joan of Arc helps lift the English siege of Orléans
events.description: French forces inspired by Joan of Arc ended the English siege of Orléans, a turning point of the Hundred Years' War. The French regained the initiative, and Joan brought Charles VII to his coronation at Reims.
events.html: French forces inspired by Joan of Arc ended the English siege of Orléans, a turning point of the Hundred Years' War. The French regained the initiative, and Joan brought Charles VII to his coronation at Reims.

events.title: Elizabeth I's Act of Supremacy receives royal assent
events.description: The Act restored the Church of England's independence from Rome and made Elizabeth its Supreme Governor. With the Act of Uniformity it formed the basis of the Elizabethan religious settlement.
events.html: The Act restored the Church of England's independence from Rome and made Elizabeth its Supreme Governor. With the Act of Uniformity it formed the basis of the Elizabethan religious settlement.

events.title: Chemist Antoine Lavoisier is guillotined in Paris
events.description: Lavoisier, executed as a former tax farmer during the Terror, had named oxygen and hydrogen and set chemistry on modern foundations. 'It took them only an instant to cut off that head,' said Lagrange.
events.html: Lavoisier, executed as a former tax farmer during the Terror, had named oxygen and hydrogen and set chemistry on modern foundations. 'It took them only an instant to cut off that head,' said Lagrange.

events.title: US and Mexican armies clash at Palo Alto
events.description: Zachary Taylor's artillery won the first major battle of the Mexican-American War near the Rio Grande. By 1848 Mexico had lost about half its territory, including California.
events.html: Zachary Taylor's artillery won the first major battle of the Mexican-American War near the Rio Grande. By 1848 Mexico had lost about half its territory, including California.

events.title: Coca-Cola goes on sale at an Atlanta pharmacy
events.description: Pharmacist John Pemberton's new syrup, mixed with carbonated water, was sold at Jacobs' Pharmacy for five cents a glass. It became one of the most widely recognised brands in the world.
events.html: Pharmacist John Pemberton's new syrup, mixed with carbonated water, was sold at Jacobs' Pharmacy for five cents a glass. It became one of the most widely recognised brands in the world.

events.title: Allies celebrate Victory in Europe Day
events.description: Germany's surrender took effect and crowds filled the streets of London, Paris and New York. In Moscow, where the surrender came after midnight, victory is marked on 9 May.

events.title: Troops fire on Buddhist protesters in Huế
events.description: South Vietnamese forces fired on crowds protesting a ban on Buddhist flags, killing nine. The Buddhist crisis that followed undermined President Ngo Dinh Diem, who was overthrown in November.
